title: Microsoft Purview: look up permissions by role and membership on the Role groups page
summary: The briefing matches the launched roadmap item, and Microsoft's documentation supports the page-access requirements, membership path and PowerShell command. It reports the conflicting documentation about default Role Management assignments and appropriately leaves the lookup's default and feature-specific details open.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; controls[0].governs
claims.claim: Role Management permits viewing, creating and modifying role groups, including membership management.
claims.quote: The Role Management role also allows you to view, create, and modify role groups. | Role Management | Manage role group membership and create or delete custom role groups. | Organization Management Purview Administrators |

claims.claim: The Purview permissions page says Role Management is assigned only to Organization Management.
claims.quote: Role Management role (assigned only to the Organization Management role group)

claims.claim: The roles reference instead names Organization Management and Purview Administrators as default holders of Role Management.
claims.quote: you need to be assigned the Role Management role, and that role is assigned only to the Organization Management and Purview Administrators role groups by default.

claims.claim: The Purview membership path is Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users.
claims.quote: On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select a Microsoft Purview role group you want to add users to. Select Edit on the control bar. On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to the selected management role group.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. The Member parameter specifies who you want to add to the role group. You can use any value that uniquely identifies the user or group. User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: The documented portal procedure for managing membership uses an admin account assigned Role Management.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal by using credentials for an admin account assigned the Role management role. Go to Settings > Roles and scopes to view and manage compliance and governance roles in your organization.

claims.claim: The documented security-group membership option is supported only in Microsoft 365 commercial cloud organizations.
claims.quote: Security groups are supported only in Microsoft 365 commercial cloud organizations.

claims.claim: Role group membership governs access to the Role groups page, rather than being a separate lookup setting.
claims.quote: To view Role groups in the Roles and scopes area in the Microsoft Purview portal, users need to be a global administrator or need to be assigned the Role Management role
